author: Book of Proverbs

author: Book of Proverbs

author: Book of Proverbs
author_lifespan: traditionally attributed to King Solomon, c. 10th century BC

author: Book of Proverbs

author: Book of Proverbs
author_lifespan: traditionally attributed to King Solomon, c. 10th century BC

author: Book of Proverbs

author: Book of Proverbs
author_lifespan: traditionally attributed to King Solomon, c. 10th century BC

text: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.
author: Book of Proverbs
author_lifespan: traditionally attributed to King Solomon, c. 10th century BC

text: In the fear of the LORD is strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge.
author: Book of Proverbs
author_lifespan: traditionally attributed to King Solomon, c. 10th century BC

author: Book of Proverbs
author_lifespan: traditionally attributed to King Solomon, c. 10th century BC

author: Book of Proverbs
author_lifespan: traditionally attributed to King Solomon, c. 10th century BC

author: Book of Proverbs
author_lifespan: traditionally attributed to King Solomon, c. 10th century BC

author: Book of Proverbs
author_lifespan: traditionally attributed to King Solomon, c. 10th century BC

author: Book of Proverbs

text: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.
author: Book of Proverbs
author_lifespan: traditionally attributed to King Solomon, c. 10th century BC

text: Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her.... Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all.
author: Book of Proverbs
author_lifespan: traditionally attributed to King Solomon, c. 10th century BC

author: Book of Proverbs
author_lifespan: traditionally attributed to King Solomon, c. 10th century BC

text: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.
author: Book of Proverbs

author: Book of Proverbs

author: Book of Proverbs

author: Book of Proverbs

text: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.
author: Book of Deuteronomy
speaker: Moses

text: But as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.
author: Book of Joshua
speaker: Joshua

text: Pray do not grieve so; but go and take a stone, and place it in the hole, and fancy that the gold is still lying there. It will do you quite the same service; for when the gold was there, you had it not, as you did not make the slightest use of it.
author: Aesop

text: Avoid a remedy that is worse than the disease.
author: Aesop
locator: The Hawk, the Kite, and the Pigeons

text: Among the many plans suggested, the one that found most favour was the proposal to tie a bell to the neck of the Cat... But when the Mice further debated who among them should thus 'bell the Cat,' there was no one found to do it.
author: Aesop

text: The foolish pair, thus hoping to become rich all at once, deprived themselves of the gain of which they were assured day by day.
author: Aesop
locator: The Hen and the Golden Eggs

text: You ridiculed the idea of my ever being able to help you, not expecting to receive from me any repayment of your favour; now you know that it is possible for even a Mouse to confer benefits on a Lion.
author: Aesop
speaker: The Mouse

text: In avoiding one evil, care must be taken not to fall into another.
author: Aesop

text: Pride goes before destruction.
author: Aesop
locator: The Fighting Cocks and the Eagle

text: Say 'I,' not 'We' are undone. He who shares the danger ought to share the prize.
author: Aesop
locator: The Two Travelers and the Axe

text: For even though you have the size of a lion among wolves, in a herd of lions you are definitely a wolf.
author: Aesop
speaker: An old Fox

text: The safeguards of virtue are hateful to those with evil intentions.
author: Aesop

text: Equals make the best friends.
author: Aesop

text: False confidence often leads into danger.
author: Aesop
locator: The Ass, the Cock, and the Lion

text: In serving the wicked, expect no reward, and be thankful if you escape injury for your pains.
author: Aesop

text: Example is more powerful than precept.
author: Aesop

text: The memory of a good deed lives.
author: Aesop
locator: The Old Woman and the Wine-Jar

text: The great do not always prevail. There are times when the small and lowly are the strongest to do mischief.
author: Aesop
speaker: The Mouse

text: Never travel with a friend who deserts you at the approach of danger. Misfortune tests the sincerity of friends.
author: Aesop
locator: The Bear and the Two Travelers

text: Everyone is more or less master of his own fate.
author: Aesop

text: It happened once that the young one which was caressed and loved was smothered by the too great affection of the Mother, while the despised one was nurtured and reared in spite of the neglect to which it was exposed. The best intentions will not always ensure success.
author: Aesop

text: How can I trust anyone as a friend who is able to fly away from his bargain whenever he pleases? Try before you trust.
author: Aesop
speaker: The Lion

text: I am treated according to my deserts. If I had only been willing to assist the Ass a little in his need, I should not now be bearing, together with his burden, himself as well.
author: Aesop
speaker: The Mule

text: I have only one; but that one is altogether a thoroughbred Lion. The value is in the worth, not in the number.
author: Aesop
speaker: The Lioness

text: I have already two oxen, who, without making any promises, do all these things. It is surely better for me to give the water to them than to you.
author: Aesop
speaker: The Farmer
locator: The Wasps, the Partridges, and the Farmer

text: Little liberties are great offenses.
author: Aesop
locator: The Lion, the Mouse, and the Fox

text: Zeal should not outrun discretion.
author: Aesop

text: The weak often revenge themselves on those who use them ill, even though they be more powerful.
author: Aesop

text: There is no believing a liar, even when he speaks the truth.
author: Aesop
locator: The Shepherd's Boy and the Wolf

text: Your feathers are all very well in the spring, but mine protect me against the winter. Fair weather friends are not worth much.
author: Aesop
speaker: The Crow

text: Evil tendencies are shown in early life.
author: Aesop
locator: The Blind Man and the Whelp

text: Hypocritical speeches are easily seen through.
author: Aesop

text: No one truly forgets injuries in the presence of him who caused the injury.
author: Aesop

text: A Lion lay in ambush in the hope of making them his prey, but was afraid to attack them while they kept together... Union is strength.
author: Aesop
locator: The Lion and the Three Bulls

text: No one can be a friend if you know not whether to trust or distrust him.
author: Aesop

text: Acquaintance softens prejudices.
author: Aesop

text: I notice that there are many prints of feet entering your cave, but I see no trace of any returning. He is wise who is warned by the misfortunes of others.
author: Aesop
speaker: The Fox

text: Do nothing without a regard to the consequences.
author: Aesop

text: Slow but steady wins the race.
author: Aesop

text: If words suffice not, blows must follow.
author: Aesop

text: O thou most base fellow? how can I believe thee, who hast disowned and wronged thy former patron?
author: Aesop
speaker: Mercury

text: I do it advisedly; for it would never do to have to sharpen my weapons just at the time I ought to be using them. To be well prepared for war is the best guarantee of peace.
author: Aesop
speaker: The Wild Boar
locator: The Wild Boar and the Fox

text: It is better for us to make friends, than to become the food of Crows or Vultures.
author: Aesop
speaker: The Lion and the Boar

text: Those who seek to please everybody please nobody.
author: Aesop
locator: The Man and His Two Sweethearts

text: The covetous are poor givers.
author: Aesop

text: A false tale often betrays itself.
author: Aesop
locator: The Fox and the Monkey (second fable)

text: The dishonest, if they act honestly, get no credit.
author: Aesop
locator: The Wolf, the Fox, and the Ape

text: Every tale is not to be believed.
author: Aesop

text: Do not be in a hurry to change one evil for another.
author: Aesop

text: These feet which would have saved me I despised, and I gloried in these antlers which have proved my destruction. What is most truly valuable is often underrated.
author: Aesop
speaker: The Stag

text: It is that men are quick to see the faults of others, and yet are often blind to their own failings.
author: Aesop

text: If you had as many brains in your head as you have hairs in your beard, you would never have gone down before you had inspected the way up, nor have exposed yourself to dangers from which you had no means of escape. Look before you leap.
author: Aesop
speaker: The Fox

text: He is not to be trusted as a friend who mistreats his own family.
author: Aesop

text: The more honour the more danger.
author: Aesop

text: Boast no more, but henceforth be content to give thy light in silence. Know that not even the stars need to be relit.
author: Aesop

text: Count the cost before you commit yourselves.
author: Aesop

text: The desire for imaginary benefits often involves the loss of present blessings.
author: Aesop

text: Some men are of more consequence in their own eyes than in the eyes of their neighbors.
author: Aesop

text: We had better bear our troubles bravely than try to escape them.
author: Aesop
locator: The King's Son and the Painted Lion

text: I learned it from the Ass, by witnessing his fate. Happy is the man who learns from the misfortunes of others.
author: Aesop
speaker: The Fox
locator: The Lion, the Fox, and the Ass

text: Do you not know that labor is the source of every blessing, and that none but those who work are entitled to eat?
author: Aesop

text: Be satisfied with half the quantity, and you will readily draw out your hand. Do not attempt too much at once.
author: Aesop

text: Youth's first duty is reverence to parents.
author: Aesop

text: In quarreling about the shadow we often lose the substance.
author: Aesop

text: Time and place often give the advantage to the weak over the strong.
author: Aesop

author: Aesop

text: Our mere anticipations of life outrun its realities.
author: Aesop

text: The greatest kindness will not bind the ungrateful.
author: Aesop

text: No arguments will give courage to the coward.
author: Aesop

text: Do not attempt to hide things which cannot be hid.
author: Aesop

text: Put your shoulders to the wheels, my man. Goad on your bullocks, and never more pray to me for help, until you have done your best to help yourself, or depend upon it you will henceforth pray in vain. Self-help is the best help.
