location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: Anybody can stop work; the trick is to start it again.
author: Andrew Carnegie
location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: It is not the rich man's son that the young struggler for advancement has to fear in the race of life, nor his nephew, nor his cousin. Let him look out for the "dark horse" in the boy who begins by sweeping out the office.
author: Andrew Carnegie
location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: If I returned to business to-morrow, fear of labor troubles would not enter my mind, but tenderness for poor and sometimes misguided though well-meaning laborers would fill my heart and soften it; and thereby soften theirs.
author: Andrew Carnegie
location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: It was such concessions as these that proved the most profitable investments ever made by the company, even from an economical standpoint. It pays to go beyond the letter of the bond with your men.
author: Andrew Carnegie
location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: A new judge is very apt to stand so straight as really to lean a little backward. Only experience teaches the supreme force of gentleness. Light but certain punishment, when necessary, is most effective. Severe punishments are not needed and a judicious pardon, for the first offense at least, is often best of all.
author: Andrew Carnegie
location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: What others could not or would not do we would attempt, and this was a rule of our business which was strictly adhered to. Also we would make nothing except of excellent quality. We always accommodated our customers, even although at some expense to ourselves, and in cases of dispute we gave the other party the benefit of the doubt and settled. These were our rules. We had no lawsuits.
author: Andrew Carnegie
location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: The surest foundation of a manufacturing concern is quality. After that, and a long way after, comes cost.
author: Andrew Carnegie
location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: She is incapable of acting or speaking rudely; all is in perfect good taste. Still, she never lowers the standard. Her intimates are only of the best. She is always thinking how she can do good to those around her.
author: Andrew Carnegie
locator: Chapter XV, Coaching Trip and Marriage
location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: The sound rule in business is that you may give money freely when you have a surplus, but your name never, neither as endorser nor as member of a corporation with individual liability. A trifling investment of a few thousand dollars, a mere trifle, yes, but a trifle possessed of deadly explosive power.
author: Andrew Carnegie
locator: Chapter XVI, Mills and the Men
location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: There is no labor so cheap as the dearest in the mechanical field, provided it is free, contented, zealous, and reaping reward as it renders service.
author: Andrew Carnegie
locator: Chapter XVI, Mills and the Men
location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: I have never since believed in being too hard on a young man, even if he does commit a dreadful mistake or two; and I have always tried in judging such to remember the difference it would have made in my own career but for an accident.
author: Andrew Carnegie
location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: If the source of my stock of that prime article, courage, were studied, I am sure the final analysis would find it founded upon Wallace, the hero of Scotland. It is a tower of strength for a boy to have a hero.
author: Andrew Carnegie
location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: Henceforth life lacks something, lacks much, my first partner in early years, my dearest friend in old age.
author: Andrew Carnegie
location: Skibo Castle, Scotland and New York (presumed)

text: Home is the place where, when you have to go there, They have to take you in.
author: Robert Frost
speaker: Warren
reference: The Death of the Hired Man (North of Boston)

text: Solidarity forever, for the union makes us strong.
author: Ralph Chaplin

text: Every child comes with the message that God is not yet discouraged of man.
author: Rabindranath Tagore

text: While there is a lower class, I am in it, and while there is a criminal element I am of it, and while there is a soul in prison, I am not free.
author: Eugene V. Debs
reference: Statement to the Court upon being sentenced

text: Nothing is more foolish than for any class to assume that progress is an attack upon it. Progress is only a call made upon it to lend its experience for the general advancement.... All of us are here together, all of us must go forward together.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter XII, Money: Master or Servant?

text: Most technical training and the average of that which we call experience, provide a record of previous failures and, instead of these failures being taken for what they are worth, they are taken as absolute bars to progress.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: A community is the better for being discontented, for being dissatisfied with what it has. I do not mean the petty, daily, nagging, gnawing sort of discontent, but a broad, courageous sort of discontent which believes that everything which is done can and ought to be eventually done better.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The best social spirit is evidenced by some act which costs the management something and which benefits all. That is the only way to prove good intentions and win respect. Propaganda, bulletins, lectures, they are nothing. It is the right act sincerely done that counts.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The moment human helpfulness is systematized, organized, commercialized, and professionalized, the heart of it is extinguished, and it becomes a cold and clammy thing.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: If an employer urges men to do their best, and the men learn after a while that their best does not bring any reward, then they naturally drop back into "getting by." But if they see the fruits of hard work in their pay envelope, proof that harder work means higher pay, then also they begin to learn that they are a part of the business, and that its success depends on them and their success depends on it.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: It is very easy, unless one keeps a plan thoroughly in mind, to get burdened with money and then, in an effort to make more money, to forget all about selling to the people what they want. Business on a money-making basis is most insecure.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: It is the business of those who plan the entire work to see that all of the departments are working properly toward the same end.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: We have no cut-and-dried places, our best men make their places. This is easy enough to do, for there is always work, and when you think of getting the work done instead of finding a title to fit a man who wants to be promoted, then there is no difficulty about promotion.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Start with an article that suits and then study to find some way of eliminating the entirely useless parts.... As we cut out useless parts and simplify necessary ones we also cut down the cost of making.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Standardization (to use the word as I understand it) is not just taking one's best selling article and concentrating on it. It is planning day and night and probably for years, first on something which will best suit the public and then on how it should be made.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter III, Starting the Real Business

text: The cost of living is a result and we cannot expect to keep a result constant if we keep altering the factors which produce the result. When we try to regulate wages according to the cost of living, we are imitating a dog chasing his tail.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Poor management can waste labour and material and nullify the efforts of labour. Labour can nullify the results of good management. But in a partnership of skilled management and honest labour, it is the workman who makes high wages possible.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: When we are at work we ought to be at work. When we are at play we ought to be at play. There is no use trying to mix the two.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Paternalism has no place in industry. Welfare work that consists in prying into employees' private concerns is out of date. Men need counsel and men need help, oftentimes special help; and all this ought to be rendered for decency's sake.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Thinking always ahead, thinking always of trying to do more, brings a state of mind in which nothing is impossible. The moment one gets into the "expert" state of mind a great number of things become impossible.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Without a profit, business cannot extend. There is nothing inherently wrong about making a profit. Well-conducted business enterprise cannot fail to return a profit, but profit must and inevitably will come as a reward for good service. It cannot be the basis, it must be the result of service.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Industry organized for service, and the workingman as well as the leader must serve, can pay wages sufficiently large to permit every family to be both self-reliant and self-supporting.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Undoubtedly the employing class possesses facts which the employed ought to have in order to construct sound opinions and pass fair judgments. Undoubtedly the employed possess facts which are equally important to the employer. It is extremely doubtful, however, if either side has all the facts.... What we really need is to get all the ideas together and construct from them.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: That which one has to fight hardest against in bringing together a large number of people to do work is excess organization and consequent red tape.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Business men go down with their businesses because they like the old way so well they cannot bring themselves to change. One sees them all about, men who do not know that yesterday is past, and who woke up this morning with their last year's ideas.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: If a device would save in time just 10 per cent. or increase results 10 per cent., then its absence is always a 10 per cent. tax.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: It is what a thing does, not what it is supposed to do, that matters. What is the use of putting a tremendous force behind a blunt chisel if a light blow on a sharp chisel will do the work?
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Why, then, if a man finds the production part of a business too much for his own two hands should he deny the title of "partner" to those who come in and help him produce?
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: It is failure that is easy. Success is always hard. A man can fail in ease; he can succeed only by paying out all that he has and is.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The producer depends for his prosperity upon serving the people. He may get by for a while serving himself, but if he does, it will be purely accidental, and when the people wake up to the fact that they are not being served, the end of that producer is in sight.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: We wanted to pay these wages so that the business would be on a lasting foundation. We were not distributing anything, we were building for the future. A low wage business is always insecure.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: We fortunately did not inherit any traditions and we are not founding any. If we have a tradition it is this: Everything can always be done better than it is being done.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: It is utterly foolish for Capital or for Labour to think of themselves as groups. They are partners. When they pull and haul against each other, they simply injure the organization in which they are partners and from which both draw support.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: A man may, by his industry, deserve advancement, but it cannot be possibly given him unless he also has a certain element of leadership.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: None of our machines is ever built haphazardly. The idea is investigated in detail before a move is made.... We are not bound by precedent but we leave nothing to luck, and we have yet to build a machine that will not do the work for which it was designed.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Better still is for the man to come through himself and exceed himself by getting rid of his fears in the midst of the circumstances where his daily lot is cast. Become a freeman in the place where you first surrendered your freedom. Win your battle where you lost it.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: If a man feels that his day's work is not only supplying his basic need, but is also giving him a margin of comfort and enabling him to give his boys and girls their opportunity and his wife some pleasure in life, then his job looks good to him and he is free to give it of his best.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: I do not believe in letting any good idea get by me, but I will not quickly decide whether an idea is good or bad. If an idea seems good or seems even to have possibilities, I believe in doing whatever is necessary to test out the idea from every angle.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: There are short-sighted men who cannot see that business is bigger than any one man's interests. Business is a process of give and take, live and let live. It is cooperation among many forces and interests.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter IX, Why Not Always Have Good Business?

text: The desire seemed to be to find a short cut to money and to pass over the obvious short cut, which is through the work.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: We have most unfortunately found it necessary to get rid of a man as soon as he thinks himself an expert, because no one ever considers himself expert if he really knows his job. A man who knows a job sees so much more to be done than he has done, that he is always pressing forward and never gives up an instant of thought to how good and how efficient he is.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: That is the way with wise people, they are so wise and practical that they always know to a dot just why something cannot be done; they always know the limitations. That is why I never employ an expert in full bloom.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter I, The Beginning of Business

text: If some man, calling himself an authority, says that this or that cannot be done, then a horde of unthinking followers start the chorus: "It can't be done."
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The man who does not get a certain satisfaction out of his day's work is losing the best part of his pay.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: If the public, the employees, and the owners do not find themselves better off because of the undertaking, then there must be something very wrong indeed with the manner in which the undertaking is carried through.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: People have too great a fondness for working with the people they like. In the end it spoils a good many valuable qualities.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: It is better to be skeptical of all new ideas and to insist upon being shown rather than to rush around in a continuous brainstorm after every new idea. Skepticism, if by that we mean cautiousness, is the balance wheel of civilization.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: If you do borrow money you are simply giving a stimulant to whatever may be wrong. You feed the disease. Is a man more wise with borrowed money than he is with his own? Not as a usual thing.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The health of every organization depends on every member, whatever his place, feeling that everything that happens to come to his notice relating to the welfare of the business is his own job.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Money comes naturally as the result of service. And it is absolutely necessary to have money. But we do not want to forget that the end of money is not ease but the opportunity to perform more service.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: All that we have done comes as the result of a certain insistence that since we must work it is better to work intelligently and forehandedly; that the better we do our work the better off we shall be.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: We eventually appointed agents, selecting the very best men we could find, and then paying to them a salary larger than they could possibly earn in business for themselves.... When we knew what our way was, we adopted the policy of paying the very highest reward for service and then insisting upon getting the highest service.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter III, Starting the Real Business

text: It is not usual to speak of an employee as a partner, and yet what else is he?... Every business that employs more than one man is a kind of partnership. The moment a man calls for assistance in his business, even though the assistant be but a boy, that moment he has taken a partner.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: If one believes that leadership brings responsibility, then a part of that responsibility is in seeing that those whom one leads shall have an adequate opportunity to earn a living.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: One of the things that we will not tolerate is injustice of any kind. The moment a man starts to swell with authority he is discovered, and he goes out, or goes back to a machine. A large amount of labour unrest comes from the unjust exercise of authority by those in subordinate positions.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Management must share the blame with labour. Management has been lazy, too. Management has found it easier to hire an additional five hundred men than to so improve its methods that one hundred men of the old force could be released to other work.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: A business ought to start small and build itself up and out of its earnings. If there are no earnings then that is a signal to the owner that he is wasting his time and does not belong in that business.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: If to petrify is success all one has to do is to humour the lazy side of the mind but if to grow is success, then one must wake up anew every morning and keep awake all day.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: Thinking first of money instead of work brings on fear of failure and this fear blocks every avenue of business, it makes a man afraid of competition, of changing his methods, or of doing anything which might change his condition.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: I never met a man who was thoroughly bad. There is always some good in him, if he gets a chance. That is the reason we do not care in the least about a man's antecedents, we do not hire a man's history, we hire the man.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Those who are below the ordinary physical standards are just as good workers, rightly placed, as those who are above.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter VII, The Terror of the Machine

text: A group of men, wholly intent upon getting work done, have no difficulty in seeing that the work is done. They do not get into trouble about the limits of authority, because they are not thinking of titles.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: I refuse to recognize that there are impossibilities. I cannot discover that any one knows enough about anything on this earth definitely to say what is and what is not possible.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: There is a pleasure in feeling that you have made others happy, that you have lessened in some degree the burdens of your fellow-men.... Good-will is one of the few really important assets of life. A determined man can win almost anything that he goes after, but unless, in his getting, he gains good will he has not profited much.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: There is perhaps no greater single source of personal dissatisfaction among men than the fact that the title-bearers are not always the real leaders. Everybody acknowledges a real leader, a man who is fit to plan and command. And when you find a real leader who bears a title, you will have to inquire of someone else what his title is. He doesn't boast about it.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: A record of failures, particularly if it is a dignified and well-authenticated record, deters a young man from trying. We get some of our best results from letting fools rush in where angels fear to tread.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: If there is any fixed theory, any fixed rule, it is that no job is being done well enough. The whole factory management is always open to suggestion, and we have an informal suggestion system by which any workman can communicate any idea that comes to him and get action on it.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: A great business is really too big to be human. It grows so large as to supplant the personality of the man. In a big business the employer, like the employee, is lost in the mass.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Rushing into manufacturing without being certain of the product is the unrecognized cause of many business failures. People seem to think that the big thing is the factory or the store or the financial backing or the management. The big thing is the product.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: When we are all in the business working together, we all ought to have some share in the profits, by way of a good wage, or salary, or added compensation.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: It ought to be the employer's ambition, as leader, to pay better wages than any similar line of business, and it ought to be the workman's ambition to make this possible.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Given a good idea to start with, it is better to concentrate on perfecting it than to hunt around for a new idea. One idea at a time is about as much as any one can handle.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter I, The Beginning of Business

text: The undirected worker spends more of his time walking about for materials and tools than he does in working; he gets small pay because pedestrianism is not a highly paid line.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The concern in which both employer and employees work to the same end of service is bound to forge ahead in business.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: I saw great businesses become but the ghost of a name because someone thought they could be managed just as they were always managed, and though the management may have been most excellent in its day, its excellence consisted in its alertness to its day, and not in slavish following of its yesterdays.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: Is business good or bad according to the dictates of fate? Must we accept the conditions as inevitable? Business is good or bad as we make it so.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter IX, Why Not Always Have Good Business?

text: He can take the direct loss on his books and go ahead and do business or he can stop doing business and take the loss of idleness. The loss of not doing business is commonly a loss greater than the actual money involved, for during the period of idleness fear will consume initiative.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter IX, Why Not Always Have Good Business?

text: An idea is not necessarily good because it is old, or necessarily bad because it is new, but if an old idea works, then the weight of the evidence is all in its favor.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: I adopted this slogan: "When one of my cars breaks down I know I am to blame."
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter IV, The Secret of Manufacturing and Serving

text: Every workman was a partner in the creation. No business can possibly be considered only with reference to to-day and to the individuals engaged in it.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: I do not believe a man can ever leave his business. He ought to think of it by day and dream of it by night.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: The employer can gain nothing by looking over the employees and asking himself, "How little can I get them to take?" Nor the employee by glaring back and asking, "How much can I force him to give?" Eventually both will have to turn to the business and ask, "How can this industry be made safe and profitable, so that it will be able to provide a sure and comfortable living for all of us?"
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: It is not necessary for the employer to love the employee or for the employee to love the employer. What is necessary is that each should try to do justice to the other according to his deserts.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The welfare of the country is squarely up to us as individuals. That is where it should be and that is where it is safest.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The men who bear titles now and are worth anything are forgetting their titles and are down in the foundation of business looking for the weak spots.... And when a man is really at work, he needs no title. His work honours him.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Dividing and subdividing operations, keeping the work in motion, those are the keynotes of production.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: One who fears the future, who fears failure, limits his activities. Failure is only the opportunity more intelligently to begin again. There is no disgrace in honest failure; there is disgrace in fearing to fail.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The thought of easy money breaks down work. There is a danger in too rapidly raising the pay of any man, whether he previously received one dollar or one hundred dollars a day.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Whoever does a thing best ought to be the one to do it. It is criminal to try to get business away from another man, criminal because one is then trying to lower for personal gain the condition of one's fellow man, to rule by force instead of by intelligence.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Very few things are ever taken under "official consideration" until long after the time when they actually ought to have been done. The buck is passed to and fro and all responsibility is dodged by individuals, following the lazy notion that two heads are better than one.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The idea is that a man must not be hurried in his work, he must have every second necessary but not a single unnecessary second.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: If he intends to remain always a manual labourer, then he should forget about his work when the whistle blows, but if he intends to go forward and do anything, the whistle is only a signal to start thinking over the day's work in order to discover how it might be done better.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: This habit of making the work secondary and the recognition primary is unfair to the work. It makes recognition and credit the real job. And this also has an unfortunate effect on the worker. It encourages a peculiar kind of ambition which is neither lovely nor productive.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Being greedy for money is the surest way not to get it, but when one serves for the sake of service, for the satisfaction of doing that which one believes to be right, then money abundantly takes care of itself.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The union of labour which is coming to the fore in this country is the union of all whose interests are interdependent, whose interests are altogether dependent on the usefulness and efficiency of the service they render.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Some organizations use up so much energy and time maintaining a feeling of harmony that they have no force left to work for the object for which the organization was created.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: No business can improve unless it pays the closest possible attention to complaints and suggestions. If there is any defect in service then that must be instantly and rigorously investigated, but when the suggestion is only as to style, one has to make sure whether it is not merely a personal whim that is being voiced.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter IV, The Secret of Manufacturing and Serving

text: The only harmonious organization that is worth anything is an organization in which all the members are bent on the one main purpose, to get along toward the objective. A common purpose, honestly believed in, sincerely desired, that is the great harmonizing principle.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: A manufacturer is not through with his customer when a sale is completed. He has then only started with his customer.... If the machine does not give service, then it is better for the manufacturer if he never had the introduction, for he will have the worst of all advertisements, a dissatisfied customer.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: The less complex an article, the easier it is to make, the cheaper it may be sold, and therefore the greater number may be sold.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter IV, The Secret of Manufacturing and Serving

text: There will never be a system invented which will do away with the necessity of work. Nature has seen to that. Idle hands and minds were never intended for any one of us. Work is our sanity, our self-respect, our salvation. So far from being a curse, work is the greatest blessing.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: It is impossible to get a product on which one may concentrate unless an unlimited amount of study is given beforehand. It is not just an afternoon's work.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter III, Starting the Real Business

text: Strength has nothing to do with weight. The mentality of the man who does things in the world is agile, light, and strong. The most beautiful things in the world are those from which all excess weight has been eliminated. Strength is never just weight, either in men or things.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter III, Starting the Real Business

text: Usually it so works out that adopting the way which is easier on the men also decreases the cost. There is most intimate connection between decency and good business.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: If you expect a man to give his time and energy, fix his wages so that he will have no financial worries. It pays.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: I was looking ahead to production, but before that could come I had to have something to produce. It does not pay to hurry.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: Certainly no business can stand outgo that exceeds its income. When you pump water out of a well at a faster rate than the water flows in, the well goes dry. And when the well runs dry, those who depend on it go thirsty.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Men will work with the idea of catching somebody's eye; they will work with the idea that if they fail to get credit for what they have done, they might as well have done it badly or not have done it at all. Thus the work sometimes becomes a secondary consideration.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: It is not a bad thing to be a fool for righteousness' sake. The best of it is that such fools usually live long enough to prove that they were not fools, or the work they have begun lives long enough to prove they were not foolish.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: I draw a plan and work out every detail on the plan before starting to build. For otherwise one will waste a great deal of time in makeshifts as the work goes on and the finished article will not have coherence.... Many inventors fail because they do not distinguish between planning and experimenting.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter I, The Beginning of Business

text: This rating system simply forces a foreman to forget personalities, to forget everything other than the work in hand. If he should select the people he likes instead of the people who can best do the work, his department record will quickly show up that fact.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: A business, in my way of thinking, is not a machine. It is a collection of people who are brought together to do work and not to write letters to one another.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Factory organization is not a device to prevent the expansion of ability, but a device to reduce the waste and losses due to mediocrity.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter XIX, What We May Expect

text: Does a man in business gain by crushing a competitor? No, destructive competition benefits no one. The kind of competition which results in the defeat of the many and the overlordship of the ruthless few must go. Destructive competition lacks the qualities out of which progress comes. Progress comes from a generous form of rivalry.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter XIX, What We May Expect

text: It is not the employer who pays wages. He only handles the money. It is the product that pays the wages and it is the management that arranges the production so that the product may pay the wages.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: We try everything in a little way first, we will rip out anything once we discover a better way, but we have to know absolutely that the new way is going to be better than the old before we do anything drastic.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Success in manufacture is based solely upon an ability to serve that consumer to his liking. He may be served by quality or he may be served by price. He is best served by the highest quality at the lowest price, and any man who can give to the consumer the highest quality at the lowest price is bound to be a leader in business.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter IX, Why Not Always Have Good Business?

text: A business is men and machines united in the production of a commodity, and both the man and the machines need repairs and replacements. Sometimes it is the men "higher up" who most need revamping, and they themselves are always the last to recognize it.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Business is never as healthy as when, like a chicken, it must do a certain amount of scratching for what it gets.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Foremen are only human. It is natural that they should be flattered by being made to believe that they hold the weal or woe of workmen in their hands. It is natural, also, that being open to flattery, their self-seeking subordinates should flatter them still more to obtain and profit by their favor.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: It is not necessary for people to love each other in order to work together. Too much good fellowship may indeed be a very bad thing, for it may lead to one man trying to cover up the faults of another. That is bad for both men.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Cutting wages is the easiest and most slovenly way to handle the situation, not to speak of its being an inhuman way. It is, in effect, throwing upon labour the incompetency of the managers of the business. If we only knew it, every depression is a challenge to every manufacturer to put more brains into his business.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter IX, Why Not Always Have Good Business?

text: The temptation to stop and hang on to what one has is quite natural.... I regarded our progress merely as an invitation to do more, as an indication that we had reached a place where we might begin to perform a real service.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter IV, The Secret of Manufacturing and Serving

text: The work and the work alone controls us. That is one of the reasons why we have no titles. Most men can swing a job, but they are floored by a title.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: You can hardly have too much harmony in business. But you can go too far in picking men because they harmonize. You can have so much harmony that there will not be enough of the thrust and counterthrust which is life, enough of the competition which means effort and progress.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The secret of it all is in a recognition of human partnership. Until each man is absolutely sufficient unto himself, needing the services of no other human being in any capacity whatever, we shall never get beyond the need of partnership.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: So long as leadership thinks more of money than it does of service, the wastes will continue. Waste is prevented by far-sighted not by short-sighted men. Short-sighted men think first of money. They cannot see waste.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The cutting edge of a factory is the man and the machine on the job. If the man is not right the machine cannot be; if the machine is not right the man cannot be. For any one to be required to use more force than is absolutely necessary for the job in hand is waste.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: If you keep on recording all of your failures you will shortly have a list showing that there is nothing left for you to try, whereas it by no means follows because one man has failed in a certain method that another man will not succeed.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: It is my ambition to have every piece of machinery, or other non-consumable product that I turn out, so strong and so well made that no one ought ever to have to buy a second one. A good machine of any kind ought to last as long as a good watch.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter III, Starting the Real Business

text: It is not good management to take profits out of the workers or the buyers; make management produce the profits. Don't cheapen the product; don't cheapen the wage; don't overcharge the public. Put brains into the method, and more brains, and still more brains, do things better than ever before.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter X, How Cheaply Can Things Be Made?

text: The man who keeps brain office hours limits his horsepower.... Leisure and work bring different results. If a man wants leisure and gets it, then he has no cause to complain. But he cannot have both leisure and the results of work.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: Scarcely more than five per cent, of those who work for wages, while they have the desire to receive more money, have also the willingness to accept the additional responsibility and the additional work which goes with the higher places.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: More men are beaten than fail. It is not wisdom they need or money, or brilliance, or "pull," but just plain gristle and bone. This rude, simple, primitive power which we call "stick-to-it-iveness" is the uncrowned king of the world of endeavour.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Progress is not made by pulling off a series of stunts. Each step has to be regulated. A man cannot expect to progress without thinking.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter IX, Why Not Always Have Good Business?

text: I think that if men are unhampered and they know that they are serving, they will always put all of mind and will into even the most trivial of tasks.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: The employer is but a man like his employees and is subject to all the limitations of humanity. He is justified in holding his job only as he can fill it.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: It could almost be written down as a formula that when a man begins to think that he has at last found his method he had better begin a most searching examination of himself to see whether some part of his brain has not gone to sleep.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: The industrious man never runs his fellow worker out of a job; indeed, it is the industrious man who is the partner of the industrious manager, who creates more and more business and therefore more and more jobs.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Concentrating on prices instead of on service is a sure indication of the kind of business man who can give no justification for his existence as a proprietor.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter IX, Why Not Always Have Good Business?

text: No man is independent as long as he has to depend on another man to help him. It is a reciprocal relation, the boss is the partner of his worker, the worker is partner of his boss. And such being the case, it is useless for one group or the other to assume that it is the one indispensable unit. Both are indispensable.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Time spent in fighting competition is wasted; it had better be spent in doing the work. There are always enough people ready and anxious to buy, provided you supply what they want and at the proper price, and this applies to personal services as well as to goods.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: The employer ought constantly to put in a harder day's work than any of his men. The employer who is seriously trying to do his duty in the world must be a hard worker. He cannot say, "I have so many thousand men working for me." The fact of the matter is that so many thousand men have him working for them.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: In the majority of cases the need of refinancing arises from bad management, and the effect of refinancing is simply to pay the poor managers to keep up their bad management a little longer. It is merely a postponement of the day of judgment.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: The creation of the body and bulk of that business is shared by everyone who has anything to do with it. No manufacturer can say: "I built this business", if he has required the help of thousands of men in building it. It is a joint production. Everyone employed in it has contributed something to it.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter IV, The Secret of Manufacturing and Serving

text: The only true labour leader is the one who leads labour to work and to wages, and not the leader who leads labour to strikes, sabotage, and starvation.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: No stunt and no advertising will sell an article for any length of time. Business is not a game.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter III, Starting the Real Business

text: I cannot say that it was hard work. No work with interest is ever hard. I always am certain of results. They always come if you work hard enough.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter I, The Beginning of Business

text: Ideas are of themselves extraordinarily valuable, but an idea is just an idea. Almost any one can think up an idea. The thing that counts is developing it into a practical product.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Where responsibility is broken up into many small bits and divided among many departments... it is difficult to find any one who really feels responsible.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: We make the individual responsibility complete. The workman is absolutely responsible for his work. The straw boss is responsible for the workmen under him. The foreman is responsible for his group.... Every man has to know what is going on in his sphere.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Waste and greed block the delivery of true service. Both waste and greed are unnecessary. Waste is due largely to not understanding what one does, or being careless in doing of it. Greed is merely a species of nearsightedness.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: Suppose you do not like a man. Is that anything against him? It may be something against you. What have your likes or dislikes to do with the facts?
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: I have always kept well within my resources. I have never found it necessary to strain them, because, inevitably, if you give attention to work and service, the resources will increase more rapidly than you can devise ways and means of disposing of them.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter III, Starting the Real Business

text: Money is not worth a particular amount. As money it is not worth anything, for it will do nothing of itself. The only use of money is to buy tools to work with or the product of tools. Therefore money is worth what it will help you to produce or buy and no more.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)
locator: Chapter II, What I Learned About Business

text: No man can view such a surplus as his own, for he did not create it alone. It is the joint product of his whole organization. The owner's idea may have released all the energy and direction, but certainly it did not supply all the energy and direction. Every workman was a partner in the creation.
author: Henry Ford
reference: My Life and Work (with Samuel Crowther)

text: You are the bows from which your children as living arrows are sent forth.
author: Kahlil Gibran
speaker: Almustafa

text: Your children are not your children. They are the sons and daughters of Life's longing for itself. They come through you but not from you, And though they are with you yet they belong not to you.
author: Kahlil Gibran
speaker: Almustafa

text: And stand together yet not too near together: For the pillars of the temple stand apart, And the oak tree and the cypress grow not in each other's shadow.
author: Kahlil Gibran
speaker: Almustafa

text: Give your hearts, but not into each other's keeping. For only the hand of Life can contain your hearts.
author: Kahlil Gibran
speaker: Almustafa

text: But let there be spaces in your togetherness, And let the winds of the heavens dance between you.
author: Kahlil Gibran
speaker: Almustafa

text: Love one another, but make not a bond of love: Let it rather be a moving sea between the shores of your souls.
author: Kahlil Gibran
speaker: Almustafa

text: You may give them your love but not your thoughts, For they have their own thoughts. You may house their bodies but not their souls, For their souls dwell in the house of tomorrow, which you cannot visit, not even in your dreams.
author: Kahlil Gibran
speaker: Almustafa

text: We now realize as we have never realized before our interdependence on each other; that we can not merely take but we must give as well; that if we are to go forward, we must move as a trained and loyal army willing to sacrifice for the good of a common discipline.
author: Franklin D. Roosevelt

text: Life has taught us that love does not consist in gazing at each other but in looking outward together in the same direction. There is no comradeship except through union in the same high effort.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupery

text: It is not your love that sustains the marriage, but from now on, the marriage that sustains your love.
author: Dietrich Bonhoeffer
reference: A Wedding Sermon from a Prison Cell (Letters and Papers from Prison)

text: Humility must always be the portion of any man who receives acclaim earned in the blood of his followers and the sacrifices of his friends.
author: Dwight D. Eisenhower
locator: Opening of address on receiving the Freedom of the City of London

text: Trust yourself. You know more than you think you do.
author: Benjamin Spock
reference: The Common Sense Book of Baby and Child Care

text: Come, Mr. Frodo! I can't carry it for you, but I can carry you.
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
speaker: Samwise Gamgee

text: United, there is little we cannot do in a host of cooperative ventures. Divided, there is little we can do, for we dare not meet a powerful challenge at odds and split asunder.
author: John F. Kennedy

text: We are caught in an inescapable network of mutuality, tied in a single garment of destiny. Whatever affects one directly, affects all indirectly.
author: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: We have inherited a large house, a great 'world house' in which we have to live together, black and white, Easterner and Westerner, Gentile and Jew, Catholic and Protestant, Moslem and Hindu, a family unduly separated in ideas, culture and interest, who, because we can never again live apart, must learn somehow to live with each other in peace.
author: Martin Luther King Jr.
reference: Where Do We Go from Here: Chaos or Community?
